name: The Holt family of Heald's company, in the fort
head: holt_isaac

present_on_scene_date.note: The family's men, women and children are on Helm's and Heald's lists of 1812-1814 (Quaife App. IV, VI).

associated_with.note: No source says which room of the fort any soldier or soldier's family lived in; the barracks named here is the reconstructed choice (liberty L-1812-people-3461).

not_in_this_household.note: A child the counts of 18 do not name may have been of this family; those children have their own reconstructed cards (hh_garrison_children_unnamed_1812).

persons.name: Isaac Holt

age_band.note: No birth year of his is recorded. A sergeant of the line was most often a man of some years' service; the band is a reconstructed choice for the figure (L418), not a claim about his age.

occupation.note: His rank as the muster-roll of the company to 31 May 1812 (Quaife 1913, Appendix VIII) prints it.

present_on_scene_date.note: An account of the battle or of its captives names him, so he was with the garrison when it marched. No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: On the muster-roll of the company to 31 May 1812 (Quaife 1913, Appendix VIII), enlisted 22 Apr 1811 for five years, to 22 Apr 1816. After 14 August: Wounded in the neck early in the action; killed in battle (Quaife).

evidence.claim: On the muster-roll of Heald's company for 20 April-31 May 1812 (row: name, rank, date of enlistment, term to, name in Present column, remark).

evidence.quote: Isaac Holt Sergeant Killed in battle
evidence.claim: Quaife's concluding table of the fate of each regular on the morning of 15 Aug 1812.

evidence.locator: Gutenberg #12183 plain text (pg12183.txt; the 1873 Philadelphia reprint of the 1856 text), line 5742-5743; ch. XIX
evidence.quote: There was a Sergeant Holt, who, early in the engagement, received a ball in the neck.
evidence.claim: Wau-Bun: Sgt Holt, shot in the neck, gave his sword to his mounted wife.

persons.name: Mrs. Holt

present_on_scene_date.note: Named in Helm's and Woodward's lists of women prisoners. No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: Wife of Sergeant Isaac Holt. First name not found. After 14 August: Mounted; fought with her husband's sword; captured; per Wau-Bun restored by a trader on the Illinois River; Quaife: possibly the woman ransomed with Mrs. Lee at Chicago. Wau-Bun (1856) believed her living in Ohio.

evidence.quote: They were Mrs. Bums wife to the citizen before mentioned as killed after the attack. Mrs. Holt, Mrs. Lee, Mrs. Needs, Mrs. Simmons.
evidence.claim: Woodward names the five women still captive.

evidence.quote: Mrs. Holt is believed to be still living, in the State of Ohio.

persons.name: The Holt child

present_on_scene_date.note: Only Quaife's reconstruction (App. IX) gives Mrs. Holt a child who survived; Helm's 'children yet in captivity' list does not mention one. No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: Child of Mrs. Holt. After 14 August: Returned with its mother (Quaife).

evidence.locator: Gutenberg #69274 plain text (pg69274.txt), line 17140-17141; Appendix IX, 'The Fated Company' (begins p. 428)
evidence.quote: One child each at least, and perhaps more, belonged to Mrs. Needs and Mrs. Holt.

evidence.quote: Two of them belonged to Mrs. Burns, and one each to Mrs. Simmons, Mrs. Holt, and Mrs. Lee.
